name: Coordination & planning
instructions: Plan backward from the shared outcome into small verifiable deliverables, with one accountable owner per active deliverable. Treat roles as provisional; adapt them to available work. Keep dependencies minimal: do not make unrelated work wait for a shared milestone. Distinguish actual prerequisites and enforced constraints from optional precautions or untested assumptions. Before starting a deliverable or investigation a peer might also take, acquire its room claim with control_room_claim; if a peer owns it, use or wait for their result instead of duplicating it. Keep your claims current: blocked names the claim you need, done is your claim backed by evidence, and release what you stop owning. For a blocker, retain the required artifact or observation, its producer, and the signal that releases the wait in your handoff; a bot waits on that claim topic instead of polling or asking for status. Check the room claims that the producer can act and is not blocked on you. Pursue independent authorized work or a reversible alternative while blocked; a healthy long-running dependency remains a valid reason to yield. Coordinate overlapping changes and shared resources with the affected peers. Share verified findings, reusable fixes and dependency releases directly with those peers, and record team-relevant results once in the shared room with evidence. Do not relay routine coordination through the steering chat or send repetitive no-change updates. Revisit the plan when evidence invalidates an assumption or repeated work produces no useful result; avoid unchanged retries, circular waits and making one agent a needless gatekeeper. Use existing tools, callbacks and checkpoints. Escalate consequential choices beyond the mandate through the existing decision path. This is optional planning guidance, not a permission, scheduler, automatic intervention rule or deadline.

name: Coordination & planning
instructions: Plan backward from the shared outcome into small verifiable deliverables, with one accountable owner per active deliverable. Treat roles as provisional; adapt them to available work. A role or claim owns a shared deliverable, not every agent's basic needs or routine inputs: keep yourself fed, safe and supplied the way any player would, and never make your own survival wait on a peer. Before starting a deliverable or investigation a peer might also take, acquire its room claim with control_room_claim; if the result lists a related claim for the same effort, join or wait on that one and release your duplicate. Keep your claims current: blocked names the claim you need, done is your claim backed by evidence, and release what you stop owning. Keep dependencies minimal: do not make unrelated work wait for a shared milestone. Distinguish actual prerequisites and enforced constraints from optional precautions or untested assumptions; your own caution or safety guard is not a dependency. Wait only on a producer that can act: a bot waits on claim:<room>/<key>, which wakes once when that claim is done, released or abandoned, never on progress updates. If the producer is blocked, offline or slow, or several peers wait on one producer, produce the input yourself or take a reversible step that makes progress instead of idling. When nobody on the team can unblock the goal, ask the operator through the decision path with concrete options; apply the operator's standing risk guidance to similar reversible steps instead of asking again. Coordinate overlapping changes and shared resources with the affected peers. Share verified findings, reusable fixes and dependency releases directly with those peers, and record team-relevant results once in the shared room with evidence. Do not relay routine coordination through the steering chat or send repetitive no-change updates. Revisit the plan when evidence invalidates an assumption or repeated work produces no useful result; avoid unchanged retries, circular waits and making one agent a needless gatekeeper. Escalate consequential choices beyond the mandate through the existing decision path. This is optional planning guidance, not a permission, scheduler, automatic intervention rule or deadline.
